# `domain/` — Domain Sub-Wiki (L0)

## Inclusion test

**Would this still be true if we canceled the product?**

If yes, it belongs here. Domain holds what is true about the world the project operates in — the shared business vocabulary, the named industry entities, the people who use products like ours, and the evidence gathered about all three. None of it is a choice this project made.

**Second test, for the evidence half: does this page need to cite anything of ours?** If yes it is not L0, however research-shaped it looks. An analysis may *name* its subject; it may not cite our `product/`, `design/`, `engineering/`, `operations/` or `gtm/` pages.

## Layer position — cited by everything, citing nothing

Domain is **L0**: it cites nothing and everything may cite it. That is the strongest constraint in the model and the reason the layer is trustworthy — a page here cannot go stale because one of our decisions changed, because it does not depend on any of them.

**L0 means *cites nothing*, not *changes rarely*.** A `mirror-source` carries the wiki's shortest freshness SLO and still sits here; an industry standard we track may move monthly. Stability of the *subject* is not the test — independence from our choices is.

## Owner

The domain function owns this sub-wiki — editorially, since most projects have no one with that title. Product and Engineering curate the vocabulary half between them; whoever runs research curates the evidence half, deciding which raw sources enter the pool and reviewing what the agent writes from them. **Authorship is not ownership:** the agent is the primary author across `sources/` and `synthesis/`, and anyone may contribute a glossary entry. Disagreements about domain language are resolved here, not scattered across other sub-wikis.

## Default origination mode: `originate`

Domain language has no better home. Unlike product content (which often lives in Linear or Notion) or design artifacts (which live in a design tool or design file), business vocabulary is frequently implicit — scattered across meeting notes, legal documents, onboarding docs, and individual mental models. The domain sub-wiki makes it explicit and canonical.

A page's `origination:` field overrides this per-page:

- `originate` (default) — the wiki IS canonical. The glossary entry, entity definition, or business rule written here is the source of truth. No external tool owns it.
- `link-only` — rare; use only when an external regulatory glossary or legal instrument is the true authority and any wiki summary would drift in a way that creates compliance risk. Even then, prefer a tight `originate` page with a citations section over `link-only`.

Almost all domain pages should be `originate`. If you find yourself reaching for `mirror`, ask whether the content genuinely belongs in another sub-wiki instead.

## In scope

The page types homed here, exhaustively. This list is the boundary, not an illustration of it — the machine-readable copy of the **Page type** column is `page-type-homes.json`, held to this list by a drift guard. The **Subdir** column is held by a different artifact — each type's own template states its home on its `Lives at:` line, and a second guard compares that line against this table. No JSON encodes a subdir; editing one of the two without the other is what the guard reports.

**Curated — the shared vocabulary:**

| Subdir | Page type | What goes here |
|---|---|---|
| `concepts/` | `concept` | Abstract ideas and mental models — bounded context, aggregate, event, policy. Also glossary entries that define a term rather than model a named instance. |
| `entities/` | `domain-object` | Named industry entities — Cart, User, Invoice, Order, Subscription. The project's own logical data-model entities are `data-model-entity` in `product/`. |
| `catalogs/` | `catalog` | An enumerated industry-governed set other pages resolve a coded value against — MCC codes, ISO country codes. A catalog of *our* statuses is L1. |
| `personas/` | `persona` | Who a person-type the industry has is. A persona our own product definition creates is a `persona` in `product/` instead. **Which of the industry's we target is a commitment**, not a fact, and lives in L1's `value-proposition`. |

**Derived — the evidence base, authored largely by the agent from `_raw/`:**

| Subdir | Page type | What goes here |
|---|---|---|
| `sources/` | `source-summary`, `mirror-source` | A summary of one raw source; or a pointer page for a source that stays canonical elsewhere. |
| `synthesis/` | `synthesis` | A cross-source pattern drawn from several inputs. |
| `interviews/` | `interview-debrief` | Research-grade notes from one customer conversation. The marketing-grade write-up of the same customer is an L5 `case-study`. |
| `comparisons/` | `comparison` | An options comparison whose subjects are external — tools, vendors, libraries. |
| `studies/` | `study` | An investigation conducted by us into an external subject; `method: market-research` here. Other methods place the study at other layers. |

The two halves carry **different authorship defaults** — curated above, derived below — which is why this table is split rather than flattened. It is not a footnote: `/wiki-ingest` and `/wiki-synthesize` write `derived` pages into `sources/` and `synthesis/` inside a sub-wiki whose other half no agent may author alone.

The subdir set grows as the sub-wiki grows. Create one when a page type first appears; never speculatively.

## Explicitly out of scope

- **Anything that cites one of our pages.** That is the second inclusion test, and it is what keeps the layer a sink.
- **Our terminology and our logical data model** — `product/`. A term this project coined is a choice, not an industry fact.
- **Decision records** — `adr` is `engineering/`, `daci-record` is `governance/`.
- **Which persona we target, our pricing, our positioning** — all commitments, all L1 or deeper.
- **An analysis of *our* process or product.** A study of how we work is `governance/`; a usability test of our surfaces is `design/`. The subject decides, not the method.

### Entity family — one concept, two persisted twins

A `domain-object` is the shared **concept** (Cart, Invoice). It is realized in persistence by the product `data-model-entity` (data a customer-facing feature operates on), while the engineering `system-entity` applies the same persisted-shape template to the platform's own system/bookkeeping data (often with no matching `domain-object`). The fuller four-way distinction — including `system-component` — lives in the engineering sub-wiki README. Two divergences are **intentional**: the concept uses prose `## Attributes` while both persisted twins use a `## Data model` table; and the concept's page path is flat (`entities/<name>` — ubiquitous vocabulary isn't module-owned) while both twins are module-scoped (`entities/<module>/<name>`).

## Templates to use

Domain pages draw from two pools: `concept`, `catalog`, `study` and `persona` come from the shared `_templates/` pool at the wiki root (populated by `/wiki-init`) because those types are valid in more than one sub-wiki; the rest ship as local page-templates under `_templates/` inside this sub-wiki.

| Template | Use for |
|---|---|
| `_templates/concept.md` (shared) | `concepts/` pages |
| `_templates/catalog.md` (shared) | `catalogs/` pages |
| `_templates/study.md` (shared) | `studies/` pages |
| `_templates/persona.md` (shared) | `personas/` pages |
| `_templates/domain-object.md` | `entities/` pages |
| `_templates/source-summary.md` | `sources/` pages summarizing one raw input |
| `_templates/mirror-source.md` | `sources/` pointer pages for a canonically-external source |
| `_templates/synthesis.md` | `synthesis/` pages |
| `_templates/interview-debrief.md` | `interviews/` pages |
| `_templates/comparison.md` | `comparisons/` pages |

To create a new page:

1. Copy the relevant template — the shared types from the root `_templates/` pool, the rest from the local `_templates/` — into the appropriate subdir.
2. Rename to `kebab-case.md` matching the page title.
3. Substitute placeholders: `{{TITLE}}`, `{{DATE}}`, `{{OWNER}}`, `{{CONFIDENCE}}`, plus any type-specific placeholders. **Exception:** every domain-local page-template (`comparison`, `domain-object`, `interview-debrief`, `mirror-source`, `source-summary`, `synthesis`) fixes `owner: domain` by construction and omits `{{OWNER}}` — do not substitute it. `{{OWNER}}` applies only to the shared-pool templates (`concept`, `catalog`, `study`, `persona`).
4. Fill the body; leave section headers even when a section is empty (use "None." or remove only if the template explicitly says to).
5. Append a `log.md` entry: `## [YYYY-MM-DD] <op> | <title>`.

## What an engine checks, and what it does not

Rules in this file fall into the classes below, and the file does not otherwise distinguish them.

- **Checked, and an error.** Cross-wiki link resolution and the layer order (`/wiki-lint`), and a page's structure against its template — sections, declared table columns, block bullets, leftover placeholders (`/wiki-conformance-audit`). These fail a run and name the page.
- **Checked upstream, against the framework rather than your page.** The type list and the Subdir column in the table above are held to their sources by drift guards that run in agent-kit's own suite, not here. You see them as a failing build in that repo, never as a finding on your wiki.
- **Not read by any engine.** The default origination mode this README states is authoring guidance, not a value anything applies to a page: a page that sets no `origination:` is never flagged for disagreeing with the default. The same is true of which subdir a page of a multi-home type belongs in, and of every cell value inside a table whose columns are checked. These are review's job.

Run the two commands for the live list; neither this section nor any other file enumerates the checks, because a list maintained beside the thing it describes is the drift this wiki keeps closing.

## Retiring or relocating a page

Neither is a hand edit, and they are different operations.

- **Retiring** a page that others cite — run `/wiki-archive`. One invocation moves the page under `_archive/`, writes the `redirect` stub at the old path so every existing link still resolves, rebuilds `index.md` and the reverse citation index, and appends the `log.md` line. Follow it with `/wiki-lint`. Never write the stub by hand: `_templates/redirect-stub.md` is the scaffold for repairing a damaged stub, and a hand-copied one names an `_archive/` path nothing moved anything to while the original page stays live — two answers at two addresses.
- **Relocating** a page that is not being retired — run `/wiki-move`. It repoints the incoming links and leaves **no** stub, because a stub for a page that still exists is a second, stale answer to the same question.

Splitting and merging carry page-local ids across; the rules are in [[_authoring:wiki-page-ids#splitting-and-merging]].

## Cross-wiki reference syntax

**Domain's allowed outbound set is empty, and that is the layer's defining property rather than an incidental restriction.** A domain page references no other sub-wiki. Provenance for an externally-established fact is carried in prose, in the `sources:` frontmatter field, or as a `[[_raw:…]]` pointer — never as a link into another sub-wiki.

This binds the templates too: no page-template homed here may *instruct* a cross-wiki citation, and a source-side lint enforces that. An analysis whose conclusions need to name an ADR, a feature or a surface is telling you it is not an L0 page.

Domain pages are a shared pool. Other sub-wikis reference domain content frequently — a product feature references the entity it acts on; an engineering ADR references the domain concept it implements.

- **Referencing domain content from another sub-wiki:** `[[domain:entities/cart]]`, `[[domain:concepts/aggregate]]`
- **Referencing within the domain sub-wiki:** omit the prefix — `[[entities/cart]]`, `[[concepts/aggregate#usage]]`
- **Anchor syntax:** `[[domain:entities/cart#lifecycle]]` — anchor matches a header slug in the target page (`## Lifecycle` here)

These are the forms most often cited across a sub-wiki boundary, not one row per directory: the link form is mechanical — `[[domain:<path-to-page>]]` — and the template table above is the complete map of which type lives in which directory. A directory with no row here is cited exactly the same way, and every sub-wiki README follows this pattern rather than indexing itself.

`/wiki-lint` validates all cross-wiki links when it is run — before a PR, or on a cadence. A broken link **or an out-of-hierarchy reference** is a lint error, not a commit block: nothing here is wired to a hook ([[_authoring:wiki-conventions#cross-reference-protocol]]).

## Typical raw sources

Content flowing into `_raw/` that this sub-wiki processes:

- Meeting notes and decision transcripts where domain terms were defined or debated
- Product briefs and strategy documents that introduce new entities or rules
- Legal and regulatory documents that define terms the product must comply with
- Existing internal glossaries or wikis being migrated
- Customer-facing documentation where canonical terminology is established
- Onboarding materials that describe the business model

Raw sources land under `<wiki.location>/_raw/` — the shared pool for the whole project. A single raw source may underpin pages in multiple sub-wikis. Cite back to the named sources via the `sources:` frontmatter field on all `derived` pages.

## When to originate vs link-only

- **Originate** for almost everything. Business vocabulary that lives only in heads or legacy documents is exactly what this sub-wiki exists to capture and make canonical. When in doubt, originate.
- **Link-only** only when an external regulatory or legal glossary is the true authority, the terms are legally binding as written in the external source, and any summarization would create compliance risk. Even in this case, prefer an `originate` page with a dedicated citations section that quotes the authoritative text and links to the external source — this is safer than `link-only` because agents and humans can read the canonical phrasing in context.

Never use `mirror` in the domain sub-wiki. If content has a canonical home in another tool, it probably belongs in a different sub-wiki (product for Linear/Notion content, operations for team tooling). Domain content that cannot be authored directly here should not be in the domain sub-wiki at all.

Some of what a page must say is not settled when it is written, and the grammar distinguishes the ways that can be true rather than collapsing them. A page whose SUBJECT has a lifecycle carries a typed `status:`. A section whose content arrives at a named later event is declared on the template's `Appends:` line and reads `Pending: <that event>.` until it does — never `None.`, which says the author considered it and had nothing to say. A page that is a register of items with their own states carries those states as columns. Which one applies is the template's to declare, not yours to choose; the full grammar is [[_authoring:wiki-page-state#page-state-axes]].
